jobs.tierReason: auto-approval policy for hand-build windows and git push; a bypass lets a session push or rewrite the repo unattended
jobs.prompt: Eleventh static security review of coordination/review/aa-new11.diff: auto-approve v1, now FILE-EDIT WINDOWS ONLY (no git capability at all: every git command stays owner-only as on main; the swarm merge standing path is unchanged). A policy window may auto-approve Write, Edit, NotebookEdit and analysed shell writes of EXACT files with extensions .md .txt .json .ndjson .csv .yaml .yml inside docs/plans, docs/state, docs/scope, docs/design and the routing notes main already allows, never tools, tests, .github, .swarm, .git, job manifests, coordination review files or the project pointer. Promises: exact-file entries only (no folder or prefix match); every written path re-checked at write time against folders and extensions; lstat-based symlink and dangling-symlink rejection; kill switch, expiry, per-window and per-day caps and stats protection on every approval path; stats initialised by the policy with a marker and never fail-open; policy file and override variables ignored outside the signed test marker; SAFE_SWARM anchored and every segment of a compound command tested; ssh and git config files protected; orchestrator mode gains nothing; git behaves exactly as on main. Previous findings (fifth review) that still apply to this scope: folder entries and code files in windows, dangling symlinks, stats never initialised, SAFE_SWARM anchoring, env overrides under the temp dir, protected files. Check each and look for NEW bypasses or fail-open paths, including: any remaining way a policy window can cover a git command or a command that runs code, a window file that is a hard link or a path reached through a symlinked ancestor, case-insensitive filesystem tricks, files inside allowed folders that other tools execute or trust (hooks, CI configs, scripts referenced from docs, package scripts), and the guard paths for shell writes (redirects, tee, sed -i, mv, cp onto a window file from a protected one). No exploit commands. Verdict PASS or FAIL, ranked findings with severity. Policy windows now cover ONLY the file tools Write, Edit and NotebookEdit of exact files under docs/state (ASCII names, .md .txt .csv .ndjson, no instruction names, full case folding); every shell command stays owner-only as on main; git and swarm merge paths are meant to be untouched. The tenth review (FAIL) found: H policy rows possibly covering Bash through covers() and activeApprovals; M XDG config protection mismatch; M protected paths compared as text without symlink resolution and list gaps; M check-to-write race only documented; M out-of-scope SAFE_SWARM and merge hunks and docs saying no deviations; L ASCII test after folding; L unreadable stats saved by the owner bump; L docs/state readers not enforced and .ndjson allowed. Verify each is fixed; list every remaining hunk that touches Bash, git, merge or safe patterns and say whether it widens or narrows what is allowed (the one known remaining merge hunk consumes the chat-merge token only when the merge is allowed); look for new bypasses in the file-tool window path and the post-write verification. Verdict PASS or FAIL; for FAIL separate blocking findings (high, or any widening of Bash, git or merge) from non-blocking ones.
